title: The mask on every table but one
outcome: Column masks were set by hand table by table; a new table with customer emails went out without one, and its files were also readable outside Unity Catalog.

content.bookmark: Masks and filters set one table at a time are only as good as the last table someone remembered. ABAC policies on governed tags cover new tagged tables automatically.

check.prompt: What is a column mask in Unity Catalog?
options: A SQL UDF that returns the real value or a masked one for each query
A copy of the table with the column removed
A privilege that hides the column from SHOW GRANTS
check.why: A column mask is a SQL UDF applied to a column at query time; it returns the value or a masked version, often based on is_account_group_member().

check.prompt: What does Databricks recommend for applying masks and filters consistently across many tables?
options: A column mask set on each table by its owner
check.why: ABAC policies attached to a catalog, schema or table, matched by governed tags, are Databricks' recommended approach for consistency; new tables with the tag are covered automatically.

check.prompt: An ABAC policy is attached to a catalog. Can a table owner inside it override the policy?
options: Yes: a table owner can drop the policy's mask on their own table at any time
No: table owners can't override the policy
Only by setting a stronger mask
check.why: Policies apply to matching tables in their scope, and table owners can't override them.

check.prompt: An external table's files are read directly from storage by another tool. Do its Unity Catalog masks apply?
options: Yes, masks travel with the files
Only for the columns that carry a governed tag, because tags are stored in the files
No: Unity Catalog privileges aren't enforced on direct file access
check.why: Direct access to an external table's files bypasses Unity Catalog, so neither grants nor masks apply.

caseStudy.setting: An online retailer (fictional) masks customer email addresses for everyone outside customer support. Each table owner adds a column mask by hand with ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN email SET MASK. A new marketing table, marketing.campaigns.recipients, is created as an external table so an outside email tool can read its files.

events.what: The marketing table goes live. Nobody adds a mask; analysts across the company can see full email addresses.
A privacy review finds the unmasked column. The owner adds the mask. The reviewer then asks what the outside email tool can see.
The answer is everything: the tool reads the Parquet files directly from storage, where Unity Catalog masks don't apply.

pipeline: Customer tables · masks added one by one by owners
marketing.campaigns.recipients · external table, no mask at first
Outside email tool · reads the table's files directly from ADLS
tasks: Why was the new table unprotected?
How should the masking be applied, and what about the outside tool?

debrief.title: Why the table was unprotected
text: Table-level masks are set by the table owner, one table at a time. The rule "emails are masked" lived in people's memory, and the new table's owner didn't know it.

Databricks recommends ABAC policies for consistency across many tables: tag the column with a governed tag (for example PII), and attach a column-mask policy to the catalog. Any new table whose column carries the tag is covered, and owners can't override it.

debrief.title: The outside tool
text: Unity Catalog's controls apply to queries through Databricks. Direct reads of an external table's files bypass them, masks included.
Give the tool only what it should see: write the recipients it needs, without the fields it mustn't have, to the location it reads, or have it query through Databricks so the policies apply.

debrief.title: Choosing the tools
text: Row filters and column masks protect one table. ABAC policies with governed tags protect every matching table. Dynamic views expose a curated slice to people without access to the base tables.
Keep mask functions simple and deterministic: Databricks' performance advice favours simple SQL UDFs with few arguments.

takeaway: Per-table masks depend on someone remembering each table.
ABAC policies with governed tags cover new tagged tables automatically.
Direct file access to external tables bypasses Unity Catalog's controls.
content.honesty: If you haven't set up data masking, say so, and explain column masks, ABAC policies and the limit of direct file access. If you have, describe how you kept it consistent.

tasks: How would you state the privacy rule so the platform can enforce it?
What should a new data product's checklist include?

debrief.title: The rule
text: "Columns tagged PII are masked for everyone except named groups", owned by privacy, enforced by a policy.

debrief.title: Checklist
text: Sensitive columns tagged; any outside system reading the data reviewed for what it can see.

sayIt.question: How do you make privacy part of building a data product?
points: Classify sensitive data when it is created.
Turn privacy rules into enforced policies, not reminders.
Check every path to the data, including outside tools.
Review new products before launch.
Give privacy a named owner.

debrief.title: Reporting
text: Take it to the privacy officer now: whether staff or the outside tool's access needs reporting is their call, not the team's.

debrief.title: Commitment
text: Policy-based masking on the customer catalog, and a review of every outside tool reading table files.

sayIt.question: Your team finds sensitive data was more exposed than intended. What do you do?
points: Contain the exposure first.
Inform the privacy or security owner straight away.
Establish what was exposed, to whom, for how long.
Fix the cause, not only the instance.
Follow the organisation's reporting process.

tasks: How do you move from per-table masks to policies?

debrief.title: The move
text: Define governed tags, tag existing sensitive columns, attach the policy at catalog level, then remove the duplicated per-table masks.

debrief.title: Tags
text: Data owners tag columns; privacy owns the tag definitions and the policy.

sayIt.question: How would you roll out a governance change across many teams' data?
points: Agree the rule and its owner.
Prepare the mechanism centrally.
Have each team classify its own data.
Switch on enforcement and verify.
Make it part of creating new data.

tasks: What would the policy look like?
How would you serve the outside tool safely?

debrief.title: The policy
text: A governed tag PII on email columns, a mask function, and CREATE POLICY ... ON CATALOG ... COLUMN MASK <function> TO `account users` EXCEPT `customer-support` FOR TABLES ... MATCH COLUMNS has_tag('PII') AS pii_col ON COLUMN pii_col.

debrief.title: The outside tool
text: Write a separate extract with only the fields the tool may have, or have it query through Databricks.

sayIt.question: Explain the options for fine-grained access control in Unity Catalog.
points: Row filters hide rows; column masks return masked values; both are SQL UDFs.
They are set per table by the owner or someone with MANAGE.
ABAC policies with governed tags apply them consistently across catalogs and schemas.
Dynamic views expose curated slices.
Direct file access to external tables bypasses all of these.
